text:
Elias Pettersson, Vancouver's No. 40 and the forward of the two players by that name, is putting up points in a season where little else around him is going right. He has 20 in 20 games, half of them on the power play, while the Canucks have lost nine of their last ten. That combination is exactly why Daily Faceoff and others are asking whether it's time to sell high on him as the club rebuilds under coach Manny Malhotra.

The case for selling is in the details. He has only 25 shots, and the quality of his own chances has dropped to 0.47 expected goals per 60 from 0.74 last season. Vancouver has also scored 5.4 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. The case against is that he carries a lot: Evolving-Hockey had his teammates in the bottom 5% and his competition in the 90th percentile last season, and the Canucks fare better with him than without at five-on-five. He's playing a harder game than his reputation, too (40 hits, 28 blocks). He's more setup man than shooter now, which works as long as someone finishes.
headline: Pettersson keeps producing as the sell-high talk grows
